summary: Modified knowledge.ts to route insight writes by store and delegate reads cross-store.

addInsight: global scope → first/default store path via getAllStores()[0]; repository scope → resolveStoreForWrite(repoName) to the store claiming the repo. Routing is inside the try block so 'not registered in any store' errors surface as isError responses.
searchInsights: delegates to getMultiStoreManager().searchKnowledge() in multi-store mode (dedup by id, store-order priority). Legacy path unchanged.
listInsights: delegates to getMultiStoreManager().listKnowledge() in multi-store mode. Legacy path unchanged.
updateInsight: iterates getAllStores() in order, applies to the first KnowledgeStoreManager that succeeds; skips 'not found' errors and continues; throws if no store has the insight.
deleteInsight: same iterate-and-match pattern as updateInsight.
All branches guarded by isStoreContextInitialized() so legacy tests continue working.
Added tests/tools/knowledge-multi-store.test.ts with 10 integration tests covering all 5 ACs.
AC3/AC4 tests pre-seed one store with a filler insight to offset the ID sequence so cross-store insights have distinct numeric IDs and are not collapsed by deduplication.
All 3787 tests pass (131 files).

comments.note: The iterate-all-stores loop in updateInsight and deleteInsight has O(n) store scans. For the common case (1–2 stores) this is negligible, but a ledger_find_insight_store() helper could short-circuit the scan. Worth revisiting if the store count grows beyond 5.

The per-store insight ID sequence starts at 1 for each store, so insights across stores collide on numeric ID. Cross-store deduplication-by-id is the correct behavior for sync scenarios, but the AC3/AC4 tests require pre-seeding one store with a filler insight to shift IDs. A global UUID or store-prefixed ID scheme would eliminate this fragility long-term.

summary: WP-009 code-review PASS. No Fix-Forward changes applied.

addInsight: single try/catch wrapping both store routing and the write operation is the cleanest possible approach. Global insights route to getAllStores()[0] with a ?? resolveLedgerRoot() fallback (defensive and correct). Repository insights route via resolveStoreForWrite() — unregistered repo errors surface naturally as isError responses.
searchInsights / listInsights: clean delegation to MultiStoreManager with in-memory tags and limit filters applied post-query, consistent with the existing legacy path behavior.

updateInsight / deleteInsight: the iterate-and-match pattern is correct and re-throws non-'not found' errors immediately — no silent swallowing of real I/O failures. The message.includes('not found') guard is a minor fragility noted as a low-priority improvement.

Tests (knowledge-multi-store.test.ts): 10 tests verify physical file placement per store (not just response shape), which is the gold standard for storage routing tests. The filler-insight workaround for ID collision is pragmatic; the underlying debt is correctly documented.

comments.note: The iterate-all-stores loop in updateInsight and deleteInsight guards 'not found' errors via message.includes('not found'). This is fragile string matching — if KnowledgeStoreManager ever changes its error message phrasing, the loop would silently misclassify a store failure as 'insight not here, try next'. A typed custom error class (e.g. InsightNotFoundError extends Error) would make this contract explicit and immune to phrasing changes. Low urgency given the error text is internal and unlikely to drift, but worth tracking.

updateInsight throws new Error(`Insight with id X not found`) after the loop, while deleteInsight re-throws lastError (preserving the original store's error message). Both produce the same user-visible text in practice, but the inconsistency means a future refactor touching one branch could diverge from the other. Aligning both to the lastError pattern would be more consistent.

[documentation-forward] The routing rule for global insights (written to getAllStores()[0] — the first store in config order, i.e., the configured default_store) is observable behavior that agents need to know. The API surface docs for ledger_add_insight should state explicitly: 'global scope writes to the default store (first in stores.json order)'. Without this, users may be surprised when auditing which store holds their global insights.
